correctness.rationale: The two-proposal weights simplify identically to \(x-aZ\tanh(cZx/a)\). Under the squared-size-biased Gaussian law, monotonicity of \(h(s)=\tanh(s)/s\) gives \(\mathbb E[Z^4h]\le3\mathbb E[Z^2h]\), hence strict conditional second-moment descent through \(c=2/3\). Gaussian Taylor expansion proves local failure beyond the threshold and the quartic coefficient \(-112/(81a^2)\) at equality. Supermartingale convergence and positive drift away from zero prove fresh-draw almost-sure convergence. The frozen scalar map has a unique symmetric locally stable cycle whenever \(cz^2>2\), with Gaussian probability \(\operatorname{erfc}(1/\sqrt c)\). The embedded verification program passed 295 finite checks; finite computations are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: A fixed antithetic Gaussian pair is a natural two-evaluation variance-reduction implementation of HJ-Prox, and retaining versus refreshing the same sample is an actionable algorithmic choice. The complete sharp conditional mean-square stability boundary, nonstandard critical quartic descent, global fresh-draw convergence and exact nonzero frozen-cycle risk jointly expose a mathematically substantive difference invisible to the contractive exact Gaussian proximal map. A low-dimensional benchmark is valuable without a general splitting theorem.
